# Public artifacts the Ledger's live-artifact verifier must check.
#
# FORMAT (one per line):   <https-url> <assertion-spec>
#
# This file names WHICH artifact to check and WHAT must be true of it. It does
# not and cannot assert that the check passed — that assertion is only ever made
# by a GitHub Actions run, from a network path we do not control, in a log a
# stranger can audit. `scripts/core/ledger.sh` reads the RESULT from the GitHub
# API, never from here.
#
# CEO ruling 2026-07-25 §7:
#   "curl from our own laptop does not count and never did."
#
# Empty list == zero artifacts to verify == `live_artifacts_verified: 0`.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ASSERTION SPECS
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#   png:<W>x<H>        HTTP 200, content-type image/png, real PNG magic bytes,
#                      and exactly those IHDR dimensions.
#   sha256:<64-hex>    HTTP 200 and the body hashes to exactly this. For
#                      immutable assets.
#   contains:<string>  HTTP 200 and the body contains this string. Minimum 12
#                      characters — short needles are rejected at discover time
#                      so nobody can satisfy a spec with `contains:<html>`.
#   echo:<param>       Strongest spec. The runner generates a fresh random nonce,
#                      appends it as `?<param>=<nonce>`, and requires it back in
#                      the response. A static placeholder CANNOT pass this. Use
#                      it for anything with real compute behind it.
#
# There is deliberately NO bare status-code spec. `https://www.snapog.dev/`
# returns HTTP 200 today and is a dead site advertising four products that all
# 404. A status check would have counted it as a live artifact. The spec must be
# something a broken or placeholder deploy would FAIL. That is the whole job.
#
# Whole-line `#` comments and blank lines only — there are no trailing inline
# comments, because `#` is legal inside a URL. A malformed line is a hard failure
# of the discover job, never a silent skip:
# a typo'd spec that quietly dropped a URL would lower the count while looking
# like a clean run.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CURRENT STATE — 2026-07-25, Cycle 4
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Empty. Nothing this company has built is deployed anywhere.
#
# `live_artifacts_verified: 0` is therefore correct and honest, and stays 0
# until a line is added below AND GitHub — not us — confirms it.
#
# Retired 2026-07-25: the SnapOG Worker URL that used to sit commented out here.
# It was blocked on CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, and the product it belonged to is
# archived (see memories/consensus.md). Its assertion, png:1200x630, is what the
# entire verifier used to hardcode.
